pages.name: Starport Encounters
pages.html:
Starport Encounters: Every six hours (or every 1D hours) spent exploring a starport, the spacers automatically engage with an encounter. Roll 1D: A 1 result is a legal encounter; otherwise they have a general starport encounter.

  • Legal encounter: This type of encounter involves the spacers being approached, questioned, or asked for permits from local law enforcement, custom agents, or security. These encounters can be avoided by rolling equal to or over the local world’s law level on the 2D + SOC DM of the spacer with the lowest SOC score in the group. Apply the NPC reaction table on pg. 56 to any legal encounters. If a legal encounter does occur, the spacers can avoid arrest, fines, etc. by making the same check again.
  • General encounter: A general starport encounter is generated by rolling a D66 on the encounter table.

Starport Encounter Modification Table: Use the Starport Encounter Modification Table to determine any modification to the tens place of the D66 roll. Combine both DMs to determine a total DM for the Starport Encounter Table. The DM is applied to the tens die.

  • For example, if a Starport B (+1) is on a world with a Captive Government (+1), then the total DM is +3. This will mean that the range on the Starport Encounter Table will be 41-96.
  • Government Code: Use the local planet’s government code on pg. 92 to determine any DMs to starport encounters.

Starport Encounter Table: A starport encounter happens while spending time in a starport between jobs. All encounters are set dressing that can be interactive if desired (unless hostile). Encounters may lead to additional adventuring situations if engaged with.

  • Remember: NPC interactions can be affected by advantage or disadvantage as determined by the Encounter Type Table.

To determine a starport encounter, roll D66 with any DM applied to the tens place. Example: +2DM would be a range from 31-86 on the following table

  • Patron encounter: Use the patron generator’s listed range for the encounter.
  • Random NPC starport encounter: Generate the random NPC using the Random NPC Table (pg. 59), using the range stated in the Starport Encounter result. The referee rolls on the NPC Demeanour table on pg. 56 with SOC DM applied to determine their reaction to the spacer.
  • Random encounter range: Some random NPC encounters will have a limited range beyond a 1D roll. A D3 roll is used to determine which 10 interval range on the table to use. For example, a random NPC result of 31-56 means you roll a D3, where a 1 is range 31-36, 2 is range 41-46, and 3 is range 51-56.

Use the Starport Encounter table on the next page

Starport Encounter Range: The following is a breakdown of what each range on the encounter table is.

  • 01-06: Abandoned or neglected
  • 11-16: Seedy
  • 21-26: Rundown
  • 31-36: Out of date
  • 41-46: Below average
  • 51-56: Average
  • 61-66: Above average
  • 71-76: Elite
  • 81-86: Prohibitive
  • 91-96: Oppressive

Book p.60
